cards.def: A burial mound of earth or stone raised over a grave or a buried treasure.
A hidden store of treasure.
A kenning for a barrow, the underground chamber inside a burial mound.
Anglo-Saxon units of land, each roughly enough to support one household.
An ornamental collar worn around the throat.
A royal woman whose marriage or presence is meant to bind two peoples in peace.
A woman whose marriage guarantees peace between two nations.
A kenning for a ship.
A kenning for a sail.
A kenning for the sun.
A kenning for the sun.
A kenning for the dragon as a creature that flies through the night sky.
A kenning for the fire-breathing dragon that scorches the land.
A kenning for the dragon as the guardian of buried treasure.
A kenning for the human body.
A kenning for the chest.
A kenning for a storm of arrows in battle.
Shields made of wood from the linden tree.
Beowulf's ancient iron-gray sword.
A line of warriors standing with their shields overlapped for protection.
The speech of the last man of a vanished people, who buries his tribe's treasure and mourns that all his companions are dead.
The passage comparing Hrethel's grief to that of an old man whose son hangs on the gallows and cannot be avenged.
A mournful poem or passage that laments death and loss.
A song of mourning for the dead.
To wail aloud in grief for the dead.
A pile of wood on which a dead body is burned.
A wooden frame on which criminals are hanged.
A spell laid by the people who buried the treasure, so that anyone who robbed it would be punished.
Being forced to leave one's lord, people, and homeland, one of the worst fates in the heroic world.
A man related by blood, to whom a warrior owes loyalty and, if he is killed, revenge.
A person who governs a kingdom on behalf of a king who is too young to rule.
A watch kept beside the body of a dead person before burial.
